title: Az-Zalzalah 99:1-3 with words spaced, and the questions
subject: Qur'an & Tajweed
unit: Summer 1: Al-'Adiyat, Az-Zalzalah and reading from the mushaf
source: Written for quran/y2 lesson 52 (Pupil PDF worksheet: Az-Zalzalah 99:1-3 with words spaced, and the questions)
intro: Lesson 52. Read each word slowly, pointing with your finger. Only the Arabic is the Qur'an; the English is a translation of its meaning.

arabic.text: إِذَا زُلْزِلَتِ ٱلْأَرْضُ زِلْزَالَهَا (١) وَأَخْرَجَتِ ٱلْأَرْضُ أَثْقَالَهَا (٢) وَقَالَ ٱلْإِنسَٰنُ مَا لَهَا (٣)

head: Ayah
Translation of the meaning (Saheeh International)
rows: When the earth is shaken with its [final] earthquake
And the earth discharges its burdens
And man says, "What is [wrong] with it?" -

keywords.def: heavy loads, what is inside the earth

questions.q: Chunk and link Az-Zalzalah 99:1-3 with the teacher.
Listening turns: today's group says 99:1-3 to the teacher, one by one. Everyone else: say it softly 3 times looking, 3 times without.
questions.a: Pupil recites with no help; the teacher marks hifdh and tajweed on the rubric and gives one target.

questions.q: Say 99:1 to 3 to a grown-up and tell them what zalzalah means.

questions.a: A) shaking. 99:1: 'When the earth is shaken with its [final] earthquake.'

questions.q: Az-Zalzalah 99:1: «إِذَا زُلْزِلَتِ ...» Which word comes next?
Think again: Have you ever felt the ground shake, or heard about an earthquake? What would it be like if the whole earth shook?
questions.a: Very frightening; Az-Zalzalah tells us about that Day, when the earth shakes and gives out what is inside it.
